Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc-Lko:22782
Court No. - 15
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 1833 of 2024

Applicant :- Ajeet Singh @ Annu Verma
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Nisha Srivastava
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
1.

Heard Ms. Nisha Srivastava, learned counsel for the accused-applicant as well as learned A.G.A.
for the State and perused the record.

2.  This is the second bail application moved on behalf of the accused/applicant- Ajeet Singh @ Annu Verma for grant of bail, in Case Crime No. 29/ 2022, under Sections 272, 302, 420, 467, 468, 471,
328, 120-B, 259, 260 I.P.C. and Section 60 (A)/ 72 of U.P. Excise Act & Section 63 of Copyright Act and Section 104 of Trade Mark Act, Police Station- Mahrajganj, District- Raebareli, during trial, as his first bail application has been rejected by this Court vide order dated 16.08.2023 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.10041 of 2022.
3. Learned counsel for the accused-applicant while pressing the bail application submits that it is a case of false implication.

articles shown to have been recovered from the possession of the applicant including the spurious liquor could also not be believed.

4. It is further submitted that applicant was not named in the first information report and his name has surfaced only in the confessional statement of the co-accused persons and on that basis, the applicant has also been roped in many other cases.

However, the same have been explained in Para No.3 of the supplementary affidavit dated 12.03.2024.
5.

It is further submitted that applicant is languishing in jail in this case since 01.02.2022 and having regard to pace, with which the trial is going on before the trial Court, the same is not going to conclude in near future and after rejection of the first bail application of the applicant, many of the co-accused persons, namely, Dhirendra Bahadur Singh, Akhand Pratap Singh @ Rajan, Dhirendra Singh, Sandeep Jaiswal, Naveen Jaiswal, Praveen Singh @ Ketan Singh, Vinay Jaiswal, Anil Jaiswal and Ram Pratap Yadav, having identical role as of the applicant have been granted bail by Coordinate Benches of this Court vide orders dated 5.2.2024, 25.1.2024, 30.1.2024, 27.2.2024,
17.1.2024, 6.2.2024, 1.2.2024, 13.2.2024 and 12.2.2024 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application Nos. 1232 of 2024, 280 of 2024, 747 of 2024, 2251 of 2024, 6375 of 2023, 9032 of 2023, 7329 of 2023, 10511 of 2023 and 12689 of 2023.
6.

It is also submitted that applicant would cooperate in the trial and would remain present before the trial Court as and when his presence would be required and thus, there is material change in the circumstances, since the rejection of the first bail application of the applicant.
There is no apprehension that after being released on bail the applicant may flee from the course of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.
7. Learned A.G.A., on the other hand, opposes the prayer of bail of the applicant on the ground that his first bail application has already been rejected by this Court.

8. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, the FIR of the case would reveal that the same was lodged by one Mathura Prasad and it is stated therein that from the licensed liquor shop of co-accused Dhirendra Singh wherein co-accused Ram Pratap is the salesman, some villagers of his Gaon Sabha had purchased liquor and they had fallen sick by consuming the same and 4 persons had died till then.
9.
It is also stated that some villagers of Ladhavamau village have also fallen sick by consuming spurious liquor.
On the day when this FIR was lodged some bottles of spurious liquor were seized from the licensed shop of Dhirendra Singh son of Chhedi Singh.

The Informant in his statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. has stated that the liquor shop is in the name of Dhirendra Singh son of Chhedi Singh but the same is managed by Dhirendra Pratap Singh son of Indra Bahadur Singh and the salesman of the shop is Ram Pratap Yadav.
10.

It is also stated by him that another shop of the locality in the name of one Mohd. Arshad Khan @ Shanu had also sold the spurious liquor and the same is managed by one Kunwar Praveen Singh @ Ketan and they in coordination are selling spurious liquor.

During the course of investigation the statements of many persons were recorded by the Investigating Officer, who after consuming spurious liquor had survived and they stated to have consumed liquor purchased from these two liquor shops.

12. Kunwar Praveen Singh in his confessional statement has stated that the applicant- Funna Pasi is the salesman of the Theka managed by him and the liquor sold from these shops were supplied to him by Naveen Jaiswal.

Dhirendra Bahadur Singh also confessed that after purchasing the spurious liquor he had gone with his son (applicant - Harshendra Singh @ Raja and Kunwar Praveen Singh @ Ketan to handover the spurious liquors bottles to the salesman Ram Pratap Yadav and after death of many persons he became scared and asked his son Harshendra Singh @ Raja and Akhand Pratap Singh @ Rajan and Kunwar Praveen Singh @ Ketan to throw the stock of spurious liquor, which was ultimately disposed of by throwing it in the Mill Area.
13.
Applicant had confessed to be associated in manufacturing and supplying of spurious liquor with other co-accused persons.

Names of some other persons like Vinay Jaiswal, Sandeep Jaiswal and Naveen Jaiswal have also surfaced who were involved in manufacturing and supplying of spurious /
poisonous liquor as well as of Shailendra Jaiswal @ Vinay and Ajeet Singh @ Annu (applicant) were arrested with Sandeep Jaiswal from the house of Sandeep Jaiswal, which was being used for manufacturing and supply of liquor.

14. Thus, it is evident from the record that the role of co-accused Funna Pasi is that he was a salesman at one of the liquor shop from where spurious liquor was sold on the fateful day and the instant applciant was involved in manufacturing/ preparing and supplying of such liquor and another co-accused person - Harshendra Singh @ Raja is the son of Dhirendra Bahadur Singh who was managing the licensed liquor shop owned by Dhirendra Singh son of Chhedi Lal and his role is confined only to the tune that he had accompanied his father (who was managing the affairs of liquor shop) when the spurious liquor was delivered to the salesman Ram Pratap Yadav and on the instruction of his father he has also disposed of surplus spurious liquor in the Mill Area.
The role of applicant is associated with regard to manufacturing of spurious liquor.

15. It appears to be an admitted fact that co-accused persons, namely, Dhirendra Bahadur Singh,
Akhand Pratap Singh @ Rajan, Dhirendra Singh, Sandeep Jaiswal, Naveen Jaiswal, Praveen Singh @ Ketan Singh, Vinay Jaiswal, Anil Jaiswal and Ram Pratap Yadav (some of whom were also involved in preparation of spurious liquor), have already been granted bail by Coordinate Benches of this Court.

The role of some of the co-accused persons, who have been granted bail subsequent to the rejection of the first bail application of the applicant by this Court, are having an identical role as of the applicant in the alleged crime.
Thus, there appears material change in the circumstances since the rejection of the first bail application of the applicant.
Criminal history of the applicant has been explained.
16. In result, the facility of bail on the principle of parity and otherwise may be extended to the applicant.
The presence of the applicant could be secured before the trial court by placing adequate conditions.

Thus, this second bail application moved by applicant is hereby allowed.

18. Let the accused/applicant- Ajeet Singh @ Annu Verma involved in above-mentioned case, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation and trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
19.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
20. Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the Court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
21. Observations made herein-above by this court are only for the purpose of disposal of this bail application and shall not be construed as an expression of this Court on the merits of the case.
Order Date :- 14.3.2024
